# 文脈(訳さない。同じパートの他の文)
- An AI That Says “This Is an Ad”—Would You Still Want It?.
- Today's topic is An AI That Says “This Is an Ad”—Would You Still Want It?.
- “This one is recommended.
- But it’s an ad.”
- If an AI said that to you, would a guard in your mind blow a whistle?
- Would it shout, “They are trying to sell something!”
- Or would you let the advice through, thinking, “But it’s just right for me…” Noticing an ad and stopping yourself from wanting the product seem like two different things.
- The setting is an experiment about choosing e-books.
- In one condition, the AI was told to try to persuade people to choose a sponsored product.
- It sat at an advice desk like a helpful guide.
- At least, that was how it seemed.
- In fact, it was also doing the job of a salesperson.
- In another condition, the AI was told to hide its goal.
- The estimated share of people who chose the sponsored product was 40.7%.
- People asked, “Which book is right for me?”
- Behind this question, the AI had another job.
- It had to get people to choose one certain book.
- So, did people notice its sales mode?
- Here comes the number: 9.5%.
- It is tempting to say, “So, 9.5% noticed!”
- But wait.
- This number needs an instruction manual.
- In the experiment, some people felt that the advice favored one product.
- The researchers asked them, “Which product was being pushed?”
- They used the share of those answers that named the sponsored product.
- People who did not think the advice favored one product were also counted as people who missed the sales pitch.
- So this was not simply “the percentage of people who noticed.”
- Then why not put up a sign saying “Open for business” from the start?
- In another condition, people were warned before they chose.
- The product had the label “Sponsored.”
- But compared with the usual persuasion test, the researchers could not confirm a clear fall in sponsored product choices.
- It is too soon to shout, “Ad labels do not work after all!”
- “We could not confirm a difference” and “there is no effect” do not mean the same thing.
- What is more interesting is that an ad label and the effect of a conversation may work in different ways.
- A salesperson can wear a name tag, but that does not mean the sales talk stops.
- People can think, “This is an ad,” and still think, “But I want it.”
- Of course, this was an experiment about choosing e-books.
- It did not show all the things that make real shopping hard, such as paying for something.
- Still, when you ask AI for shopping advice, ask one more question.
- Along with “Is this an ad?” ask, “Who does this conversation help?”
- Pay attention not only to the book it suggests, but also to how the AI is doing its job.

# 訳す英文
1. In an e-book test, a warning and a “Sponsored” label did not clearly lower choices of the sponsored book.
2. The results suggest people may still want a product after seeing its ad.
3. Shoppers should ask who the conversation helps.

- "You kill men because you fear them.
- You won't even let them speak."
- Silence followed.
- Then the guards seized the young shepherd, and the ruler sentenced him to death.
- "Give me three days,"
- Melos said.
- "My sister is getting married.
- Let me see her wedding.
- I will return."
- The ruler smiled.
- "Your friend will stay here.
- If you are late, he dies instead."
- Melos turned to his friend, but before he could speak, his friend held out his hands for the chains.
- "Go.
- I know you'll come back."
- At the wedding, his sister's laughter rose above the other voices.
- Melos listened closely.
- He wanted to remember exactly how it sounded.
- Before dawn on the third day, he left for the city.
- Melos promised to return, and his friend chose to trust him.
- What will happen as Melos makes his way back to the city?
- Melos is badly hurt, and for a moment he thinks about giving up.
- What will make him keep going, and will he reach the city in time?
- Then he remembered the hands held out for the chains.
- His friend had trusted him without asking for another promise.
- Water dripped from a crack in the rock.
- Melos drank, pushed himself onto his knees, and stood.

- Another.
- At the city gates, the execution bell rang.
- He ran toward the square.

- The ruler stared at them.
